text:
Maya: hey all, first day! :wave: M2 Mac mini. switched to fish, cloned dotfiles and trying to use asdf + direnv for envs. python and node installs fail initially — turned out asdf shims weren't on PATH in the GUI apps (VS Code), and I hit an openssl configure error for python. Also curious about proxy settings: corporate HTTP proxy drops off in containers unless I export http_proxy in devcontainer. who should I ping for Okta/1Password/git access? any fish+direnv tips?

DevX: welcome Maya! couple quick things:
- GUI apps (VS Code) on mac don't inherit shell PATH by default. either launch VS Code from terminal (code .) or add the asdf init line to ~/.config/fish/config.fish so GUI shells pick it up via login shell.

DevX: sample fish lines I use: 
```
# asdf & direnv for fish
eval (asdf init - | source)
status --is-interactive; and direnv allow || true
# ensure asdf shims earliest in PATH for GUI apps
set -x fish_user_paths (asdf where)/shims $fish_user_paths
```
That puts asdf shims first.

Carlos: re: openssl on Apple Silicon, we recommend Homebrew OpenSSL but also pass CONFIGURE_OPTS so the build won't try system libs. I do: 
```
brew install openssl@3 pkg-config
set -x BREW_OPENSSL (brew --prefix openssl@3)
env CONFIGURE_OPTS="--with-openssl=$BREW_OPENSSL" asdf install python 3.11.7
```
Also if you see `error: gnutls` or crypto linkage issues, check that PKG_CONFIG_PATH points to the brew openssl pkgconfig.

DevX: for nodejs plugin, sometimes GPG import fails behind a proxy. if curl complains, download the keyring on another network or use `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=true` temporarily and re-import (but prefer a non-insecure route).

Maya: thanks, launching code from terminal fixed the PATH problem and asdf shims show up. used BREW_OPENSSL + CONFIGURE_OPTS and python built. node failed earlier because my ~/.gnupg dir had wrong perms (gpg refused the key import). fixed with `chmod 700 ~/.gnupg` then re-ran the import, node installed.

Carlos: good catch on .gnupg perms.

DevX: about proxies and devcontainers: add the http_proxy/https_proxy entries to devcontainer.json config env or use `~/.docker/config.json` for daemon-level proxy. We have a sample in the handbook at docs/onboarding/proxy-setup.md.

IT: Maya 3 - for Okta/1Password/Git access open a ticket at https://itsupport.redwood.internal/new or reply here with manager email + employee id and I'll escalate. Typical turnaround < 2 business days.

onboard_bot: Checklist created for Maya: [create-ssh-key, add-to-1password, clone-dotfiles, install-asdf-runtimes, setup-direnv, request-vpn] (0/6).

Maya: Okta invite incoming, 1Password pending. quick follow-up: any preferred pattern for direnv + asdf? I want per-project runtimes to auto-activate.

DevX: use a .envrc that loads asdf: `use asdf` is available via direnv-asdf integration if you have the plugin; otherwise put `layout python` / `layout node` and add `asdf local python 3.11.7` to repo. We store common .envrc snippets in the dev handbook.

Maya: great, set local runtimes and direnv allow worked. thanks everyone :heart:
